subject: science
passage: Many moths fly toward artificial lights at night, and in cities this behavior can be costly: moths that circle streetlights are easily eaten by predators and spend less time feeding and mating. Researchers in Switzerland collected young ermine moths from areas with heavy light pollution and from areas with dark night skies and raised all of them from the larval stage in identical laboratory conditions. When the adults were tested, moths from the light-polluted populations were noticeably less likely to fly to a light than moths from the dark-sky populations. Because the moths had been raised under the same conditions, the results suggest that ______
stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.A: the urban moths' weaker attraction to light is likely inherited, not learned.
choices.B: streetlights have no effect on the survival of moths that live in large cities.
choices.C: moths from dark-sky areas will soon lose their attraction to light as well.
choices.D: moths that avoid lights are less able than others to find food at night.

explanation.why: Since all the moths grew up in identical conditions, a difference between them cannot easily be explained by their surroundings during their lives. The text also says that moths drawn to lights in cities are more likely to be eaten and to mate less. Together, these points suggest that city populations have come to inherit a weaker attraction to light.
explanation.A: Correct. Identical rearing rules out learning from surroundings, so the difference is most likely inherited.
explanation.B: Incorrect. The text says flying to streetlights is costly for city moths, the opposite of having no effect.
explanation.C: Incorrect. Nothing in the text predicts a change in moths from dark areas, where lights are rare.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The text says moths that circle lights spend less time feeding, not that moths avoiding lights do.
